question: Can a query-independent Panoramax sequence, bound to the same exact OSM entrance node, transport a discriminative pixel field onto a ray-consistent functional portal in a second sequence while rejecting every wrong entrance reference?

cohort.selection_provenance: The four lowest candidate indices remaining after exclusions that expose at least two strict DIRECT views from distinct Panoramax collections. Selection used provider and OSM metadata only; no selected image pixels, DINO fields, or portal proposals were observed.
cohort.view_pair_rule: Within every eligible collection choose the strict DIRECT item nearest 40 metres to the entrance, tie by item id. Choose the cross-collection pair with the smallest absolute distance difference, then lexicographic collection and item ids. The lexicographically first collection is reference and the other is query.

viewport.projection: deterministic equirectangular-to-rectilinear remap centered on the strict entrance ray

model.backend_rule: Profile the frozen DINOv2 workload once on available CPU and CUDA candidates through the project research backend, then use the measured selection for all eight viewports.

representation.target_field: Frozen reciprocal native-grid DINO matches, partial-affine RANSAC consistency, strongest same-node reference support, and strongest wrong-node support subtraction.
representation.portal_proposals: Frozen PortalLatticeConfig defaults; no threshold, family, or Top-K tuning on this cohort.
representation.binding: Frozen SupportFieldConfig defaults. A target token requires a unique COMMIT proposal that contains the projected entrance x coordinate and is retained in portal Top-3.
representation.wrong_goal_test: Each query is replayed against all three other entrance references. Any wrong-goal COMMIT or SET_VALUED candidate containing the projected entrance x coordinate is a false binding.

stop_condition: Run one frozen replay. If the gate is not met, do not tune DINO, viewport, portal lattice, binding thresholds, candidate order, seed, or fusion on these pixels; change the entrance credential or portal information source.
claim_boundary: A pass is a four-entrance cross-sequence Development mechanism result: an exact-node-conditioned public reference observation transports discriminative pixels to a unique ray-consistent functional portal while wrong entrance references stay rejected. It is not independent pixel annotation of the exact door, legal or public access, traversability, collision-free motion, metric waypoint or arrival, HANDOFF_READY, product benefit, user benefit, or safety evidence.
